messages:
alex.k: hey @people-ops quick question — i'm an international new hire (starting next week). i don't have a SSN yet. what do i need to get payroll + benefits set up? can payroll run without SSN? also trying to enroll my spouse as dependent for health — they don't have a SSN either. who should i send docs to?

marta.hr: congrats and welcome, alex! :tada: quick answers: we can start payroll without SSN in most cases but payroll needs a placeholder ID and additional paperwork while you apply for an ITIN/SSN. for benefits, dependents can often be enrolled with passport and marriage certificate if SSN is pending — we'll confirm with benefits vendor.

josh.payroll: tagging in payroll details. alex, please: 1) complete the new hire forms in Rippling (W-4 + direct deposit). for direct deposit, you can enter bank info but note "SSN pending" in the comment field. 2) upload proof of identity (passport) and proof of address to the secure HR folder (link below). 3) once you have ITIN/SSN, notify us and we'll update retroactively if needed.

lina.ops: link to secure upload: https://redwood-secure/upload — pick "new hires" then "alex.k" folder. for spouse docs: scanned passport + marriage certificate usually works (pdf). if vendor asks for SSN later, we'll handle the follow-up.

alex.k: thanks! one more — are there any tax-withholding implications i should expect before SSN? worried about incorrect withholding rates.

josh.payroll: short answer: withholding may be at a default rate until we have completed the appropriate forms (ITIN/SSN). we'll set your federal/state withholding as best effort from your W-4. if too much is withheld, payroll/corp will process adjustments/refunds once we have correct info.

payroll-bot: FYI — new-hire checklist created for alex.k. tasks: verify ID docs, set temporary payroll record, enroll benefits pending SSN. Owner: josh.payroll. Due: 3 business days.

alex.k: perfect. what about reimbursements for relocation expenses? can i submit receipts now?

marta.hr: yes — submit all receipts to Expensify and tag the trip as "Relocation - New Hire". include a short note with dates and purpose. expense policy requires itemized receipts; if you paid with cash, add a short explanation. we can advance certain approved expenses if needed — tell us amount and we'll expedite.

lina.ops: quick Expensify guide snippet: ```Category: Relocation
Project: NewHire-Relocation
Attach: airfare, hotel, receipts
Annotate: travel dates + purpose```

alex.k: got it — i'll upload docs tonight. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

marta.hr: great — ping me once uploads are in, i'll review and loop in benefits vendor if anything missing. welcome again!
